plan: This is a second-price auction where I pay the second-highest bid if I win. In this format, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value ($24). Bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth to me if I win at a high second-highest bid. Bidding lower risks losing auctions I could have profitably won. Since payment depends on others' bids, not mine, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit regardless of competitors' strategies.

This is a second-price auction where the winner pays the second-highest bid. In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value, regardless of what others do. Bidding my true value ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the market price (second-highest bid) and never overpay, while avoiding losses from bidding too high. With no prior history to inform deviations, truthful bidding is optimal.

This is a second-price auction where the winner pays the second-highest bid, not their own bid. In this format, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value, as bidding higher risks overpaying beyond my value, and bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. Since my value is $13, I should bid $13 to maximize expected profit regardless of other bidders' strategies.
